oh-start.speaker: S01
oh-start.narration: Oliver Hale doesn't get up. He waves his glass at the chair opposite.
oh-start.text: Let me guess. The prodigal son, drowning in debt, steals Daddy's favourite toy. It's very neat. It's also rubbish.

choices.label: Ask where he was last night

oh-night.speaker: S01
oh-night.text: The Regency, till three. I lost, since you ask. The doorman will remember me; I tip badly when I lose.

oh-collection.speaker: S01
oh-collection.text: Forty years of polishing cars nobody drives, while the roof leaks. I want him to sell. He'd rather sell me. That's the whole family history.

oh-tommy.speaker: S01
oh-tommy.text: Tommy? Devoted. He drove me to school for years. He cried this morning, did you know? Stood in the empty bay and cried. More than my father did.

oh-e007.speaker: S01
oh-e007.text: All right. I had the spare key for the afternoon. I had the car photographed for a sale brochure. Behind his back, yes. It was back in its bay by ten past seven and the key was back at Marco's by half past. Ring Fenwick's studio.

oh-e006.speaker: S01
oh-e006.text: You've been through my letters. Yes, I owe the Regency. If I'd stolen that car I'd have paid them this morning, wouldn't I?

oh-unmoved.speaker: S01
oh-unmoved.text: No idea. Should that mean something to me?

mf-start.speaker: S02
mf-start.narration: Marco Ferri talks with his hands, and his hands are black with grease.
mf-start.text: Fifteen years I've kept that car alive. Fifteen years! And he owes me eight months. But I'd sooner steal the Pope's hat than that car.

choices.label: Ask how you'd move that car without a sound

mf-service.speaker: S02
mf-service.text: Oil, plugs, and the handbrake cable. It used to stick. Now it releases clean. I told Tommy, because Tommy's the one who moves her.

mf-quiet.speaker: S02
mf-quiet.text: You don't start her. You take the handbrake off and she rolls. That drive slopes all the way to the lane. But you'd need to know the brake was fixed, and the only man I told was Tommy.

mf-key.speaker: S02
mf-key.text: The spare's on hook twelve. Oliver signed it out Saturday afternoon, said his father wanted photographs. It came back by half seven. Look at the card.

mf-unmoved.speaker: S02
mf-unmoved.text: That's paperwork. I don't do paperwork. Ask my wife.

tr-start.speaker: S03
tr-start.narration: Thomas Reece sets a cup of tea in front of you on a saucer, with a biscuit.
tr-start.text: Six years I've looked after that car, Detective. I found the bay empty at seven and I just stood there. I'll help any way I can.

variants.narration: There's a smell of burnt paper in the flat that wasn't there before.
variants.text: Kingsway can say what they like, Detective. I've nothing to hide. Ask what you want.

choices.label: Ask who holds the alarm codes
Ask whether he saw anything on the lane
Bluff: tell him the transport firm has already talked

tr-night.speaker: S03
tr-night.text: Bed at eleven, up at six. Came down at seven for the Sunday polish, like every Sunday. I never heard a thing. That's what I can't get over.

tr-codes.speaker: S03
tr-codes.text: Mr Hale and I. That's all. But anyone could have watched one of us put it in. Anyone at all.

tr-oliver.speaker: S03
tr-oliver.text: I shouldn't say. Master Oliver owes money to some unpleasant people. And he had the spare key on Saturday. I'm only telling you what I know.

tr-lane.speaker: S03
tr-lane.text: Now you mention it, Mr Pryce's Bentley was on the lane last night. Quarter to twelve, engine running. I saw the lights from my window before I turned in.

tr-bluff.speaker: S03
tr-bluff.narration: He goes very still. Then he smiles.
tr-bluff.text: Have they. Well. Then you won't be needing anything from me, will you? Excuse me a moment, I've left something on the stove.

tr-e003.speaker: S03
tr-e003.narration: The cup rattles in its saucer.
tr-e003.text: Code three. That... someone must have seen me put it in. They must have. I was asleep.

tr-e013.speaker: S03
tr-e013.text: A lorry driver in the dark? He'd say anything for a fiver. I was asleep, I tell you.

tr-e012.speaker: S03
tr-e012.narration: He reads his own name on the job sheet, and something in his shoulders gives.
tr-e012.text: They said nobody would ever know. Nine thousand pounds, Detective, and they said they'd come round and discuss it in person.

tr-e010.speaker: S03
tr-e010.text: That's my business. A man's allowed a bet on a Saturday.

tr-e011.speaker: S03
tr-e011.text: Dealers write to chauffeurs all the time. We know the cars. It doesn't mean anything.

tr-unmoved.speaker: S03
tr-unmoved.text: I'm sorry, Detective, I don't know anything about that. More tea?

pc-start.speaker: S04
pc-start.narration: Philippa Crowe folds the racing pages without hurrying.
pc-start.text: I doubled the valuation on Tuesday and it walked on Saturday. I know exactly how that looks, Detective, so let's skip the part where you tell me.

variants.text: You haven't read my report, have you? It's in your file. Read it, then ask me something I haven't already written down.

choices.label: Ask how cars like this disappear

pc-val.speaker: S04
pc-val.text: Two of the other three Castellanes changed hands this spring for over a hundred and fifty. His policy was five years out of date. Any assessor would have done the same.

pc-how.speaker: S04
pc-how.text: Within a day they're on a ferry. Nobody drives a car like that across the country; it goes on a transporter at night. And there's only one firm in Ridgeway that does night pickups and takes cash: Kingsway, out on the ring road.

pc-family.speaker: S04
pc-family.text: The son's in debt to people you don't owe money to. The father's too ill to notice. If you want a motive in that house, you won't have to look far.

pc-e014.speaker: S04
pc-e014.text: Owner and chauffeur, codes one and three. I recommended a second holder and a camera on the lane. Nobody listened. They never do.

pc-unmoved.speaker: S04
pc-unmoved.text: Not my department, I'm afraid. I value them. I don't find them.

dp-start.speaker: S05
dp-start.narration: Desmond Pryce doesn't rise, but he does lower his newspaper.
dp-start.text: I suppose you've heard what I said at the club. 'One way or another.' A figure of speech, Detective. I buy cars. I don't steal them.

choices.label: Ask where he was last night
Ask who'd buy a car like that without papers

dp-car.speaker: S05
dp-car.text: Chassis four of four. I own two and three. I offered Augustus a hundred and fifty thousand, five times. He'd rather it rotted than sell it to me.

dp-night.speaker: S05
dp-night.text: Here, all evening. I slept upstairs. I never went near Ashgrove Road.

dp-buyers.speaker: S05
dp-buyers.text: There's a dealer in Rotterdam, Van der Berg, who'll take anything with a famous chassis and no questions. He writes to chauffeurs and mechanics, not owners. They're the ones with the keys.

dp-e005.speaker: S05
dp-e005.narration: He folds the newspaper very small.
dp-e005.text: I drove out to make one last offer. In person, like a gentleman. I sat at his gate for ten minutes and couldn't bring myself to ring the bell at midnight like a drunk. I was back here by twenty past. Ask the porter.

dp-unmoved.speaker: S05
dp-unmoved.text: I don't see what you want me to say about that.
